Paella Valenciana (Chicken & Shrimp)

55 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Simmering the Saffron Rice

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Bomba or short-grain paella rice65g130g195g260g
Chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into pieces100g200g300g400g
Large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tail-on60g120g180g240g
Chicken stock200ml400ml600ml800ml
Saffron threads8 threads16 threads24 threads32 threads
Olive oil8ml16ml24ml32ml
Onion, diced25g50g75g100g
Garlic cloves1234
Roma tomato, grated (or crushed tomatoes)25g50g75g100g
Red bell pepper, sliced20g40g60g80g
Sweet paprika⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Frozen peas15g30g45g60g
Lemon wedges1234

Steps

  1. Steep the saffron threads in 2 tablespoons of warm stock for 10 minutes to bloom their color and aroma.
  2. Season the chicken with salt and brown it in olive oil in a wide paella pan 6-8 minutes, turning once, until deeply golden. Remove to a plate.
  3. In the same pan, cook the onion, garlic, and red pepper 5 minutes until softened.
  4. Stir in the grated tomato and paprika, cooking 3-4 minutes until jammy and slightly darker.
  5. Add the rice and stir 1-2 minutes to coat every grain in the sofrito.
  6. Return the chicken to the pan, pour in the stock and saffron mixture, stir once to distribute evenly, then do not stir again.
  7. Simmer uncovered over medium heat 10 minutes, then reduce to low and cook 8-10 minutes more, until the rice is nearly tender.
  8. Nestle the shrimp into the rice and scatter the peas on top. Cook 5 minutes more until the shrimp are pink and opaque.
  9. Raise the heat for the last 1-2 minutes to form a crispy bottom layer (the socarrat), listening for a light crackle.
  10. Rest 5 minutes, covered loosely with foil, then serve straight from the pan with lemon wedges.

Tortilla Española (Spanish Potato Omelette)

45 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Confit-Frying the Potatoes

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Yukon gold or waxy potatoes, peeled, thin-sliced150g300g450g600g
Onion, thinly sliced40g80g120g160g
Eggs2468
Olive oil (for confit-frying, most drained off)100ml200ml300ml400ml
Saltto tasteto tasteto tasteto taste

Steps

  1. Peel and thinly slice the potatoes (about 3-4mm); thinly slice the onion.
  2. Heat the olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the potatoes and onion, and season with salt.
  3. Confit gently, stirring occasionally, 20-25 minutes, until the potatoes are fully tender but not browned.
  4. Drain the potatoes and onion in a colander over a bowl, reserving the oil. Let cool 5 minutes.
  5. Beat the eggs in a large bowl with a pinch of salt.
  6. Fold the drained potato-onion mixture into the beaten eggs and let sit 5 minutes.
  7. Heat 1-2 tablespoons of the reserved oil in a small nonstick skillet (18-20cm) over medium heat.
  8. Pour in the egg-potato mixture, spreading evenly, and cook 2-3 minutes until the edges set.
  9. Slide onto a plate, invert the pan over it, and flip both together so the tortilla drops back in uncooked-side down. Cook 2-3 minutes more, until just set but still soft in the center.
  10. Slide onto a plate, rest 5 minutes, and slice into wedges to serve warm or at room temperature.

Gambas al Ajillo (Garlic Shrimp)

20 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Raw Shrimp and Sliced Garlic

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Large shrimp, peeled and deveined100g200g300g400g
Olive oil30ml60ml90ml120ml
Garlic cloves, thinly sliced36912
Dried chili flakes (or ¼ dried guindilla)⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Dry sherry or dry white wine15ml30ml45ml60ml
Lemon juice½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Fresh parsley, chopped5g10g15g20g
Crusty bread, for serving1 slice2 slices3 slices4 slices
Saltto tasteto tasteto tasteto taste

Steps

  1. Pat the shrimp dry and season lightly with salt.
  2. Combine the olive oil, sliced garlic, and chili flakes in a cold skillet.
  3. Set over medium-low heat so the garlic warms gradually with the oil, 2-3 minutes, until fragrant and just turning golden — don't let it brown.
  4. Raise the heat to medium-high and add the shrimp in a single layer.
  5. Cook 1-2 minutes per side until the shrimp turn pink and opaque.
  6. Pour in the sherry and let it bubble and reduce by about half, roughly 30 seconds.
  7. Squeeze in the lemon juice and season with salt.
  8. Remove from heat and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
  9. Serve immediately, still sizzling in the pan, with crusty bread for dipping.

Pollo al Ajillo (Garlic Chicken)

40 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — A Generous Handful of Peeled Garlic

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Bone-in chicken thighs, cut into pieces150g300g450g600g
Olive oil15ml30ml45ml60ml
Garlic cloves, whole, peeled481216
Dry white wine30ml60ml90ml120ml
Bay leaf¼½¾1
Fresh thyme sprig¼½¾1
Fresh parsley, chopped3g6g9g12g
Salt and black pepperto tasteto tasteto tasteto taste

Steps

  1. Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper.
  2. Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat.
  3. Brown the chicken skin-side down 5-6 minutes until deep golden, then flip and brown the other side 4-5 minutes. Remove to a plate.
  4. Lower the heat to medium-low and add the whole garlic cloves to the same pan.
  5. Cook the garlic gently 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and softened but not burnt.
  6. Pour in the white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
  7. Return the chicken to the pan with the bay leaf and thyme; bring to a simmer.
  8. Cover partway and simmer 15-18 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink near the bone.
  9. Uncover and simmer 2-3 minutes more to reduce the sauce slightly.
  10. Sprinkle with parsley and serve with crusty bread or roasted potatoes.

Albóndigas en Salsa (Spanish Meatballs in Tomato Sauce)

45 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Rolling the Meatballs

Meatball Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Ground beef60g120g180g240g
Ground pork60g120g180g240g
Egg¼½¾1
Dried breadcrumbs, soaked in milk10g20g30g40g
Milk (for soaking breadcrumbs)15ml30ml45ml60ml
Garlic clove, minced½11½2
Onion, finely grated15g30g45g60g
Fresh parsley, chopped3g6g9g12g
Ground cuminpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp¼ tsp
Sweet paprikapinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp¼ tsp
Olive oil (for frying meatballs)15ml30ml45ml60ml

Sauce Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Onion, finely diced20g40g60g80g
Garlic cloves1234
Roasted red pepper, chopped15g30g45g60g
Crushed tomatoes100g200g300g400g
Dry white wine15ml30ml45ml60ml
Bay leaf¼½¾1
Stock (chicken or beef)30ml60ml90ml120ml

Steps

  1. Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes until softened.
  2. Combine the ground beef, pork, soaked breadcrumbs, egg, garlic, grated onion, parsley, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Mix gently until just combined.
  3. Roll into golf-ball-sized meatballs and chill 15-30 minutes to firm up.
  4. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the meatballs in batches, 2-3 minutes per side, until golden all over. Remove to a plate.
  5. In the same pan, cook the diced onion 4-5 minutes until soft.
  6. Add the garlic and roasted red pepper, cooking 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
  7. Pour in the white wine and let it reduce by half, scraping up any browned bits.
  8. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, stock, and bay leaf; bring to a simmer.
  9. Return the meatballs to the sauce, cover partway, and simmer 20-25 minutes, until cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
  10. Taste, adjust the salt, discard the bay leaf, and serve with crusty bread or over rice.

Fabada Asturiana (Bean & Chorizo Stew)

2 hrs (+ overnight soak)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — The Compango (Chorizo, Morcilla & Tocino)

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Dried large white beans (fabes), soaked overnight60g120g180g240g
Spanish chorizo (cured, for cooking)40g80g120g160g
Morcilla (Spanish blood sausage)30g60g90g120g
Pork belly or salt pork (tocino)30g60g90g120g
Garlic cloves1234
Onion30g60g90g120g
Bay leaf¼½¾1
Smoked paprika (pimentón)⅛ tsp¼ tsp⅜ tsp½ tsp
Saffron threadspinchpinchsmall pinchpinch
Stock or water300ml600ml900ml1200ml
Saltto tasteto tasteto tasteto taste

Steps

  1. Soak the dried beans in plenty of cold water overnight, at least 8 hours; drain before cooking.
  2. Put the soaked beans in a large pot with the chorizo, tocino, whole garlic cloves, onion, and bay leaf.
  3. Cover generously with cold stock and bring slowly to a bare simmer — never let it boil hard, or the bean skins split.
  4. Skim off any foam that rises to the top.
  5. Stir in the saffron and smoked paprika, partially cover, and simmer very gently 1.5-2 hours, until the beans are completely tender and creamy, adding a splash of cold water if it threatens to boil too hard.
  6. About 20 minutes before the beans are done, add the morcilla so it doesn't fall apart from overcooking.
  7. Once tender, lift out the chorizo, morcilla, and tocino, slice, and return to the pot.
  8. Season the broth with salt to taste — it should be thick enough to lightly coat a spoon.
  9. Let the stew rest off the heat 10 minutes before serving.
  10. Ladle into bowls with beans, broth, and a bit of each meat, plus crusty bread on the side.

Patatas Bravas with Alioli (Dinner Combo, with Crusty Bread)

40 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Pounding the Garlic Alioli

Potato & Brava Sauce Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Yukon gold or russet potatoes, 2cm cubes150g300g450g600g
Olive oil (for frying/roasting potatoes)30ml60ml90ml120ml
Onion, finely diced (for brava sauce)20g40g60g80g
Garlic cloves (for brava sauce)1234
Crushed tomatoes60g120g180g240g
Smoked paprika¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Cayenne pepperpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp¼ tsp
Sherry vinegar¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Olive oil (for brava sauce)10ml20ml30ml40ml

Alioli Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Garlic clove½11½2
Egg yolk¼½¾1
Olive oil30ml60ml90ml120ml
Lemon juice¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Crusty bread, for serving1 slice2 slices3 slices4 slices

Steps

  1. Soak the cubed potatoes in cold water 20-30 minutes, then drain and pat completely dry.
  2. Fry or roast the potatoes (220°C/425°F), turning occasionally, 20-25 minutes, until deeply golden and crisp outside, tender inside.
  3. Meanwhile, warm olive oil in a saucepan, add the onion, and cook 4-5 minutes until soft.
  4. Add the garlic, cook 1 minute, then stir in the smoked paprika and cayenne, cooking 30 seconds to bloom the spices.
  5. Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer 10-12 minutes until thickened; stir in the sherry vinegar and season with salt.
  6. For the alioli, whisk the minced garlic with the egg yolk and a pinch of salt.
  7. Whisking constantly, add the oil in a thin, slow stream, then a bit faster once thickened, until glossy and mayonnaise-like.
  8. Whisk in the lemon juice and season with salt to taste.
  9. Drain the crisped potatoes and pile onto a plate.
  10. Spoon the warm brava sauce over the potatoes, drizzle with alioli, and serve with crusty bread as a full dinner plate.

Crema Catalana (Bonus)

25 min (+2 hrs chill)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Torching the Sugar Crust

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Whole milk125ml250ml375ml500ml
Egg yolks1234
Granulated sugar (for custard)15g30g45g60g
Cornstarch4g8g12g16g
Lemon peel (strip, no pith)¼½¾1
Orange peel (strip, no pith)¼½¾1
Cinnamon stick¼½¾1
Granulated sugar (for caramelized top)8g15g23g30g

Steps

  1. Pour the milk into a saucepan with the lemon peel, orange peel, and cinnamon stick.
  2. Warm gently until steaming but not boiling, then remove from heat and steep 10-15 minutes. Strain out the peels and cinnamon.
  3. Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until pale, then whisk in the cornstarch until smooth.
  4. Slowly pour a little of the warm milk into the yolk mixture, whisking constantly to temper the eggs.
  5. Pour the tempered mixture back into the saucepan with the rest of the milk.
  6. Cook over low heat, whisking constantly, 5-8 minutes, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
  7. Pour into shallow ramekins or terracotta dishes and cool to room temperature.
  8. Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, until fully chilled and set.
  9. Just before serving, sprinkle an even layer of sugar over each custard.
  10. Caramelize with a kitchen torch (or hot broiler for 1-2 minutes) until deep amber and crackly, then serve immediately.
